value.text:
The National Institute of Technology Karnataka (NITK), also called NITK Surathkal, is a public technical university in Surathkal, Mangaluru, in the Indian state of Karnataka. It was formerly Karnataka Regional Engineering College (KREC), and is described as one of India's National Institutes of Technology and an Institute of National Importance. Its suburban campus lies near the Arabian Sea along National Highway 66. The article describes a 295.35-acre campus with residential, library, computing, sporting and other student facilities.

The foundation stone for KREC was laid on 6 August 1960. The original engineering courses covered mechanical, electrical and civil engineering, under affiliation with the University of Mysore. Postgraduate teaching began in 1966, and the college transferred affiliation to Mangalore University in 1980. On 26 June 2002, the institution was elevated to National Institute of Technology status and adopted the NIT Karnataka name. These dates describe different stages of the same institution rather than separate universities.

NITK offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral education, with programs across engineering, science and management. Its academic account lists 14 departments and 11 support centres, and gives approximate figures of 5,500 students, 200 faculty members and 300 support staff without a clear reporting year. A January 2020 memorandum with the Indian Space Research Organization proposed a Regional Academic Centre for Space; its announcement alone does not demonstrate that the centre was subsequently established.
